name: Pump-in sub
function: A stack section with a side port for pumping fluid into the stack or bleeding pressure off it, used for pump-down, equalizing, and bleeding down before rig-down.

tabs.overview: A short tube with a hammer union or flanged side outlet; a valve on the port is closed during the run unless pump-down fluid is delivered through it.
tabs.engineering: Rated with the stack; port size 2 in. typical.
tabs.safety: The port line is a live high-pressure line while pumping; it is restrained and bled before disconnection.
tabs.evidence: Public pressure control equipment catalogs and service descriptions (S6, S7, S13); API RP 67 (S14) and API RP 19B (S15) for the perforating side; field practice (S9).

hazards.control: Pressure test the stack before opening the swab valve; bleed to zero before breaking any union.
Stay clear of the cable path, sheaves, and the top of the stack while the string is moving.
